title.en: Linear equations in two variables and their graphs

text.en: A courier charges Rs 10 plus Rs 5 per kg. The cost y = 5x + 10 relates weight x and cost y. Each (x, y) pair that fits is a solution; together they lie on a straight line.

A linear equation in two variables has the form ax + by + c = 0 with a and b not both zero.
It has infinitely many solutions (x, y); each solution is a point on its graph.
To graph it, find at least two (better three) solutions, plot them and draw the straight line through them.
The line x = 0 is the y-axis and y = 0 is the x-axis; x = k is a vertical line and y = k a horizontal line.
Putting x = 0 gives the y-intercept, and y = 0 gives the x-intercept.
A point lies on the line only if its coordinates satisfy the equation.
Two such equations together make a system, and their common solution is where the two lines meet.

text.en: A linear equation in two variables has the form ax + by + c = 0 with a and b not both zero.
It has infinitely many solutions (x, y); each solution is a point on its graph.
To graph it, find at least two (better three) solutions, plot them and draw the straight line through them.
The line x = 0 is the y-axis and y = 0 is the x-axis; x = k is a vertical line and y = k a horizontal line.
Putting x = 0 gives the y-intercept, and y = 0 gives the x-intercept.
A point lies on the line only if its coordinates satisfy the equation.
Two such equations together make a system, and their common solution is where the two lines meet.
If x = 0 then y = 4, so (0, 4) is on the line. If y = 0 then x = 2, so (2, 0) is on the line.
A third point: x = 1 gives y = 2, so (1, 2) lies on it too.

why.en: A third point checks the line.

text.en: Plot the three points; they lie on one straight line. Draw it with arrowheads.

why.en: The line extends in both directions.

prompt.en: How do you draw the graph of a linear equation in two variables?

points.en: ax + by + c = 0 has infinitely many solutions.
Its graph is a straight line.
x = 0 gives the y-intercept; y = 0 the x-intercept.
A point on the line satisfies the equation.
